title: Diwali Chhath Bus Ticket Booking Guide for 2026
summary: A step by step booking guide for Diwali and Chhath 2026, covering how early to book, which routes sell out first, what to check at checkout.
body_markdown:
The honest answer depends less on the calendar than on your route. A corridor with twenty daily departures forgives a late booking. A corridor with three does not, and most of the routes that matter in November sit closer to the second category than the first.


# What This Diwali Chhath Bus Ticket Booking Guide Covers


Diwali falls on Sunday, 8 November 2026 and the main Chhath arghya on Sunday, 15 November, which creates two outbound waves and two return crunches inside a single fortnight of travel.


Rather than repeating the calendar, this runs through the booking itself as a sequence of nine decisions, from choosing dates to what to check at checkout. Live availability for any corridor sits on the[zingbus route and city pages](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets) for your travel date.


## A Practical Diwali Chhath Bus Ticket Booking Guide


Most festive booking advice stops at telling people to book early, which is not useful on its own. This Diwali Chhath bus ticket booking guide works through the specific steps where trips actually go wrong, in the order you encounter them.


### Step 1: Fix the Return Date Before the Outbound One


Outbound demand spreads over two or three evenings. Return demand collapses onto one or two, because almost everyone is going back to the same working Monday. That asymmetry is the single most useful thing to understand.


Decide your return date first and book it in the same session as the outbound leg. A one way booking with an open return is how people end up on a 3 AM departure or a train waitlist in the middle of a festival week.


### Step 2: Check How Many Daily Buses Your Route Actually Runs


Before deciding when to book, look at how many services your corridor has. The number sits on every route page, and it changes the urgency completely.


**Route profile** **Typical daily departures** **Booking window that still leaves choice**


Major metro corridor Ten or more Two to three weeks before travel


Long intercity route Three to ten Three to four weeks before travel


Thin or single operator route One to three Four to six weeks, and earlier if dates are fixed


The thin routes are the ones that carry most festive travellers home, because home is usually a smaller town. If your corridor has three buses a day, treat the last week of October as your deadline rather than a suggestion.


### Step 3: Book Inside the Window That Still Has Range


Fares on private intercity services move with how much of a specific bus has sold, so the useful question is not whether prices will rise but whether the range you want still exists. Early in the cycle you can choose between a budget seater and a premium sleeper. Late in the cycle the choice is usually one remaining berth.


**Note:** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


### Step 4: Use the Filters Instead of the First Result


The default sort is rarely the right bus for a festive trip. Three filters do most of the work.


- Departure time: a bus leaving before the evening peak clears the city faster than one leaving at 10 PM on a festival eve.
- Bus type: for journeys over seven hours, a sleeper is worth the difference, particularly if you are heading into a family day on arrival.
- Boarding point: filter to the pickups you can actually reach, then compare only those services.


### Step 5: Choose the Seat, Not Only the Bus


The seat map is where a good booking becomes a comfortable journey. Lower berths are easier for elders and anyone travelling with a child. A 2+1 layout gives a single berth with more width on one side. Seats over the rear axle move more on rough sections, which matters on a nine hour run.


Women only seats can be selected at checkout on zingbus services, which is worth using for solo overnight travel. Seat maps also show how full a bus already is, and that is a better signal of how fast the route is filling than any general advice.


### Step 6: Pick a Boarding Point You Can Reach in Festive Traffic


A pickup that is convenient in September may be unreachable on the evening before Diwali. Terminal counters are the steadier choice in peak weeks because they are easy to find in a crowd and are not dependent on a connecting cab crossing the city.


Reaching the boarding point 20 to 30 minutes early is a small habit that prevents the most avoidable festive problem of all, which is watching your bus leave while you are three streets away.


### Step 7: Check Offers and Meals Before You Pay


Coupons and payment offers are applied at checkout rather than automatically, so the payment step is worth a moment of attention. Current promotions are listed on the[zingbus offers page](https://www.zingbus.com/offers-all) .


Two meal options exist and they are different things. Freemeal is a route specific offer that applies on Plus buses on Delhi to Lucknow, Delhi to Gorakhpur and Chennai to Coimbatore, applied through the relevant coupon code. Food on Bus is a separate paid service where you pre-book a vegetarian meal during checkout or later from the My Trip section of the app, with items priced from about Rs 99, served at your seat by the marshal.


### Step 8: Read the Cancellation Terms Before You Commit


Festive plans change more often than ordinary ones, and the time to understand what a change costs is before you pay rather than after. The current terms are set out on the[zingbus policies page](https://www.zingbus.com/policies) .


For travellers who make the same trip several times a year, zingprime adds cancellation flexibility that may be worth evaluating against your own pattern. Assess it on how often you travel rather than on one festival trip.


### Step 9: Save What You Will Need on Travel Day


Keep the e ticket accessible offline, since network coverage at a crowded terminal is unreliable. Note the marshal will verify an OTP before boarding, so keep the booking phone with you. Save the support number, which is +91 82870 09889 on WhatsApp, and check baggage against the 15 kg per passenger limit before you leave home rather than at the bus door.


## If Your Route Already Shows Sold Out


Three things are still worth trying. Shift the departure by one day, because the evening before a festival is far tighter than the festival day itself. Look at a nearby boarding city, since a corridor from Noida, Ghaziabad or Gurgaon may have availability that the Delhi listing does not. Or break the journey, travelling to a large hub such as Lucknow and booking the shorter second leg separately.


What rarely works is waiting for a cancellation to appear on a peak festive night. Seats do release, but not reliably enough to plan a family trip around.


## Turning the Checklist Into a Booked Trip


Nine steps sounds like a lot until you realise most of them take under a minute. The ones that genuinely decide how the trip goes are the first two, because the return date and the number of daily departures together tell you exactly how much time you have left.


Work out those two answers this week. If your corridor runs three buses a day and you need to be home on 7 November, the rest of this booking guide is only useful if you act on it before the last week of October.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How early should I book bus tickets for Diwali 2026?


Book two to three weeks ahead on major corridors and four to six weeks ahead on thin routes, since Diwali falls on 8 November 2026.


### How early should I book for Chhath 2026?


Book by the last week of October for Chhath, which runs from 13 to 16 November 2026 with the main arghya on Sunday, 15 November.


### Which leg of the trip is harder to book?


The return leg is harder to book, because outbound travel spreads across several evenings while returns concentrate on one or two dates.


### Why does this Diwali Chhath bus ticket booking guide start with the return date?


This Diwali Chhath bus ticket booking guide starts with the return date because return seats are scarcer, and leaving them open causes most festive travel problems.


### Do bus fares increase during the festive season?


Fares move with demand and remaining availability rather than a fixed festive tariff, so the cheaper options simply sell out earliest on peak nights.


### Which routes sell out first around Diwali and Chhath?


Routes with only one to three daily departures sell out first, especially those serving smaller towns in eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.


### Is a sleeper or a seater better for festive travel?


A sleeper suits journeys over seven hours, particularly when you arrive in the morning and head straight into a full family day.


### Can I change my boarding point after booking?


Changes are handled case by case through customer support and depend on seat and route availability, so raise any request as early as possible.


### What should I check at the payment step?


Check any applicable coupon or payment offer, whether a meal option applies to your route, and the cancellation terms attached to your fare.


### What is the luggage limit on zingbus?


The luggage limit is 15 kg per passenger, which is easy to exceed during festival travel when you are carrying sweets and gifts.


### What can I do if my route is sold out?


Shift your travel by a day, try a nearby boarding city such as Noida or Ghaziabad, or break the journey through a larger hub.


### Are women only seats available?


Women only seats can be selected at checkout on zingbus services, which is worth using for solo overnight travel during crowded festive weeks.


### How early should I reach the boarding point?


Reach the boarding point 20 to 30 minutes early during festive weeks, since terminals are crowded and departures do not wait for delayed passengers.
